ID: `better-accessibility`.

## What it does

Walks through the experience first with a keyboard and then with a screen reader, when available. Checks control names and states, native HTML elements, dialog focus, errors associated with fields, dynamic announcements, target sizes and motion. Verifies that content remains reachable with zoom and narrow screens. Contrast and colors are measured with better-colors.

## When to use it

Use it to examine a complete flow, form, menu or dialog, especially when the experience must work without a mouse. Reading code can reveal some defects but does not replace testing with a keyboard and screen reader.

## How to use it

Ask for it by name, or invoke it with `/better-accessibility` in Claude Code or `$better-accessibility` in Codex. Specify the flow, components, states and devices to cover. Request issues ordered by severity, with location, consequence and correction. If you authorize changes, keep them within the project system and retest affected behaviors.

## What it delivers

- Findings with severity and location
- Corrections based on semantics and behavior
- Outcome and checks not performed

## Example

Check the invitation dialog: opening, initial focus, Tab, Escape, return to the button and email field errors.
